FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

A landmark day for Aston Villa brings about a trip to Ipswich, who will be keen to get back to winning ways at Portman Road.

Match News and Current Form

It’s been a solid start to life back in the Premier League for Ipswich, but things have shown signs of unravelling in recent weeks on the back of a five-match winless run (D2, L3). Successive defeats against Bournemouth and most recently Tottenham leave the Tractor Boys in a precarious position, and in order to improve their fortunes, they’re likely to have to shore up their defence having conceded in their last 30 Premier League games. The outright record in the competition stands at 34 matches, but conceding hasn’t been too detrimental at home as they’ve picked up three of their four competitive wins there this term despite conceding in each. 

Aston Villa make the long journey to Suffolk for their 5000th game in the top four tiers of English football (W2050, D1199, L1750), just the 16th team in history to reach that milestone. They perhaps couldn’t have wished for a better game to mark the occasion, as Villa are unbeaten in all 22 Premier League games against promoted opposition under Unai Emery (W15, D7). Stretching that seems likely for a Villa side in the midst of a seven-game unbeaten league run (W3, D4), although a midweek defeat against Galatasaray in the UEFA Champions League sees them come into this clash on a downer.

Head-to-Head History

Ipswich have won just one of the 12 Premier League H2Hs (D4, L7), while they haven’t won a home league game against Villa since September 1984 (D6, L5 since).

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Only Hull (114) have had fewer shots than Ipswich (120) in the Premier League this season.

Ipswich have scored half of their home league goals this season after the 80th minute (3/6).

Aston Villa conceded all four of their second-half away league goals this season after the 80th minute.

Aston Villa have kept eight first-half clean sheets in the Premier League this term.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Ipswich’s Jack Clarke has been mainly limited to opportunities off the bench this season, but could still make an impact having seen six of his last seven goals arrive after the 70th minute. Aston Villa’s Boubacar Kamara is never far away from the action having racked up a pre-round league-high 50 foul involvements this season (fouls committed: 24, fouls drawn: 26).

Ipswich’s Leif Davis picked up an ankle issue last weekend, while Villa have no fresh concerns and could welcome back Matty Cash.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Villa’s record against promoted opposition is formidable, so backing an away win here looks the best route to take. 

Author: Chris Wilson
